sentences.text: The Mid-Day Meal Scheme is a government initiative aimed at enhancing the nutritional status of school-age children.
It was launched in 1995 and is one of the largest school meal programs in the world.
The primary objective is to provide cooked meals to children in primary and upper primary schools.
This scheme aims to improve school enrollment and attendance while also addressing child malnutrition.
Benefits include the provision of nutritious meals to children which helps in their physical and mental development.
The scheme also encourages parents to send their children to school.
Eligibility includes children enrolled in government and government-aided schools.
The application process typically involves school authorities registering students under the scheme.
Meals are provided on all school days.
The implementing authority is the Ministry of Education in collaboration with state governments.
Local bodies such as panchayati raj institutions may also be involved in the implementation.
The scheme is funded by the central and state governments.
Monitoring and evaluation are conducted to ensure quality and effectiveness.
